title: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

sentences.text: Has a leap second ever been taken away?
The IERS table of atomic time against civil time only ever climbs: 10 seconds in 1972, 37 since 2017, 27 single-second steps up and not one back.
sentences.note: 37 is the size of the gap, not a count of leap seconds: the table opens at 10 seconds in 1972 and reaches 37 in 2017, so the 27 steps between are the leap seconds, every one of them an addition.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has been added to civil time; none has ever been taken away: the IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds on 1 January 1972 to 37 seconds on 1 January 2017, each value one second larger than the last, 27 steps in all.
